requirements.requirement: Run LDAP on node1 for dc=branch,dc=test and import the staged identities and mail addresses unchanged.
requirements.summary: The staged LDIF contains the branch suffix, people OU, Alex North/alex@branch.test, and Sam West/sam@branch.test. The final live search returned the same two records and count after node1 restarted, with slapd active and enabled.

requirements.requirement: Node2 can search the people subtree and find both users.
requirements.summary: Direct searches originating on node2 returned both complete user records and a count of two before and after the node restarts.

requirements.requirement: Directory updates require authenticated administrator access and anonymous writes fail.
requirements.summary: An anonymous add was rejected with LDAP result 8, while an authenticated Directory Manager successfully added, read, and deleted a test entry. Administrator authentication and anonymous rejection were reconfirmed after restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use legacy-platform-compatible software.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained RHEL 7.9 on kernel 3.10.0-1160.el7.x86_64, and the installed LDAP components are OpenLDAP 2.4.44-22.el7 packages.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is also complete on both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart observation, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered LDAP service or client/data behavior. The only notable deficiency is cleanup hygiene.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so the evidence cannot independently establish overall package-database health.
The lifecycle inventory covers bounded locations and observations; it does not provide an exhaustive filesystem diff, including direct confirmation of the retained configuration backup directories.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required service, firewall rule, packages, data, and client remained functional, with no failed services observed. Hygiene was reduced by abandoned temporary installation and test artifacts on both nodes. The failed direct-RPM attempts left downloaded RPMs behind (cmd-44001a78cc1b446e, cmd-4b5ca0f285054c54); repository/key files and numerous LDAP test LDIF/output files also remained after their bounded prerequisite or evidence roles (cmd-eda7842c0c4849a0, cmd-829e3eaa40d34855, cmd-3b10a8d85e624a54, cmd-da19782351554246, cmd-4480b56601854fb2). A failed initial generated-config attempt was removed by the corrective import command, so that mutation was reverted, while the superseded bad-password configuration backup appears to have been retained (cmd-21f01da97255455b, cmd-752fd68103d14c11, cmd-432f590875654f32). These were bounded and low-risk but not cleaned up.
